questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Interesting city, great location in the heart of Europe, well-known and good university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Had an amazing time, met interesting people from around the world, lived very central. The city has a lot to offer and is very livable

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. I received all necessary information from the university. My Wohnheim helped me as well. It was all straight forward.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had trouble getting the courses I had gotten pre-approved, but everything worked out in the end. Benedict the erasmus coordinator at LMU was quick at replying.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy. If you want cheap housing through the uni then prioritize Oly-Dorf. So many exchange students live there. I did not get any housing offers and I was lucky to find something else. My tip is checking out/monitoring WG gesucht and reach out a lot.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I liked it, but be careful about locations. Make sure there is a Ubahn or similar close to the place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Since I did not get any housing through uni that question is difficult to answer.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Stressful. My tip is to reach out and be proactive in getting the courses that you want/need. I e-mailed a professor to get his permission to take his course (it was a masters course and I am a bachelor student) and then forwarded that mail to the Erasmus coordinator to be able to take that course. Maybe it made a difference, I do not know. In the end, however, my own experience and my friends' experiences are that it works out. You can change things even after the deadline if you are just proactive.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A very large guide document was send to the incoming students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful. I got the ones I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Trust the proces, be proactive and then it will be fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very class-room oriented which was nice but different from KU. The exam form is oral presentations and not written papers which I disliked, but it was very easy to prepare for an exam because you just had to preprare for the subject of that particular week and not have an overview of the whole curriculum.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Medium. Lower level than at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Class-room teaching, a lot of class discussions and opinions. It was a very active type of learning compared to KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Contemporary Spanish Politics
Conflict in African Countries: Causes and Consequences
The Political System of the European Union
Challenges of Democracy in Modern Contemporary Societies 
Democratic Development and Stability in Germany

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I recommend this or anything with Stefan Matern: Challenges of Democracy in Modern Contemporary Societies
I do not recommend Conflict in African Countries: Causes and Consequences
In English courses you find exchange students and mostly not in the German courses. Make up with your self which type of friends you see youself having and choose courses accordingly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: ZHS sport provides a lot of very cheap sports courses. ESN MESA arranges events in the whole semester.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ZHS sport provides a lot of very cheap sports courses. ESN MESA arranges events in the whole semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Oktoberfest and trips with the Deutschlandticket

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Garmisch, skiing, Prague, Vienna, Salzburg

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy but I still learned a lot

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak german and reach out. They are not as closed as you might think.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Bavarian culture, cuisine and the language

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Start looking for housing early. Have an open mind and say yes to everything in the beginning. Go to Oktoberfest. Try to find local friends. Take advantage of all the native speakers and insist on improving your German! Do a german course in the month before the semester starts. That is a way to make friends and learn the language - I highly recommend this.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met. There were no other Danish people in my friends group and I enjoyed the multicultural dynamics. And also the city is great and has a lot to offer.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting the right courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
